::: {.block title="Introduction"}
Satellites see chlorophyll only near the surface, but phytoplankton, and the
food webs and carbon export they support, extend through the water column and
often peak below it. In the open ocean, ocean color can predict that profile
(@fig-examples). We ask two new questions: does hyperspectral PACE do better
than a multispectral sensor, and does the approach work in coastal water?

![Observed (black) and predicted (blue dashed) CHLA for four open-ocean BGC-Argo profiles, drawn at random within each peak-depth class. Predictions are from models that saw no data from the profile's 1° cell within its 30-day block.](figures/fig_example_profiles.png){#fig-examples script="scripts/fig_example_profiles.py" width="100%"}
:::
